facts.statement: The name Laornis translates to "stone bird" derived from Ancient Greek words for stone and bird.
facts.quote: Laornis means "stone bird", from Ancient Greek lao "stone" + ornis "bird".

facts.statement: The species name edvardsianus honors the French paleontologist Alphonse Milne-Edwards for his work on fossil birds.
facts.quote: edvardsianus honors Alphonse Milne-Edwards, to compliment the French paleontologist on his landmark study Recherches Anatomiques et Paleontologiques pour servir a l'Histoire des Oiseaux Fossiles de la France

facts.statement: Fossils of Laornis were found in the Hornerstown Formation in Pemberton Township, New Jersey, United States.
facts.quote: It was found in Late Cretaceous or Early Paleocene sediments of the Hornerstown Formation at the Birmingham Marl Pits, Pemberton Township, New Jersey, United States (39°59'N, 74°43'W).

facts.statement: The sediments containing Laornis fossils were deposited approximately 66 to 63 million years ago.
facts.quote: The deposits were laid down at approximately 66–63 Ma (million years ago).

facts.statement: Based on its fossil bone, Laornis is thought to have been a semi-aquatic bird with a body size at least that of a large goose.
facts.quote: Its general shape suggests that Laornis was a semi-aquatic bird with longish legs and a body at least the size of a large goose.

facts.statement: If Laornis was a wading bird, it likely stood about one meter (3 to 4 feet) tall.
facts.quote: It may have been a wading bird, in which case it stood probably around one meter (3–4 ft) tall in life

facts.statement: Laornis has been variously allied with the orders Charadriiformes and Gruiformes and is tentatively placed in its own family, Laornithidae.
facts.quote: It has variously been allied with the Charadriiformes and the Gruiformes, and is tentatively placed in a family of its own, Laornithidae.

facts.statement: Laornis might have belonged to the extinct family of stilt-legged waterfowl known as Presbyornithidae.
facts.quote: It might have been one of the extinct stilt-legged waterfowl of the Presbyornithidae

facts.statement: It is possible that Laornis was an ancient pseudotooth bird, a group of seabirds with unclear affiliations.
facts.quote: it cannot even be excluded that it was an ancient pseudotooth bird, seabirds of unclear affiliation that evolved to immense proportions in the Neogene

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Laornis as Graculavidae.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Laornis within the family Graculavidae.
The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Laornis as the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus Laornis is known from a single fossil specimen, a tibiotarsus leg bone discovered in the late 19th century.
rejected.quote: Laornis is a genus of a prehistoric neornithine birds, known only from Specimen YPM 820, a single tibiotarsus leg bone discovered in the late 19th century.

rejected.statement: Alternatively, Laornis may have been a larger seabird with proportionally shorter legs.
rejected.quote: On the other hand, it might have been a larger seabird with proportionally shorter legs.
